title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

reports.title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

summary:
Rebecca Green agreed to have an AI scribe transcribe her first urologist appointment in Australia. After kidney stone surgery, she read a letter from the specialist to her GP that falsely said she micro-dosed psychedelic mushrooms, which she had never done. The error upset her and worried her because she was receiving workers' compensation and feared illegal drug claims could hurt her case. She complained, and the urologist apologised, corrected the record, and said she would review how AI was used in her practice.

A Digital Rights Watch report found similar AI scribe mistakes, including recording the wrong breast in a cancer diagnosis and inventing epilepsy. The Royal Australian College of GPs estimates about 40 percent of GPs regularly use AI scribes. Australia's medicines regulator, the TGA, says no AI scribes are approved and some may be breaking the law. It will release findings in coming weeks and act on breaches. The report calls for approved tools to be tested and published.
